title: Find the Minimum Area to Cover All Ones I
statement: `grid` is a rectangular matrix in which every cell holds `0` or `1`, and at least one cell holds `1`. Look at rectangles laid along the grid lines, so their sides run parallel to the rows and columns of `grid`, that contain every cell holding a `1`. Return the smallest area such a rectangle can have, where the area is its number of rows times its number of columns.
notes:
## Intuition

A rectangle covers every `1` exactly when its top row is at or above the highest `1`, its bottom row at or below the lowest one, and likewise for the leftmost and rightmost `1`. Shrinking any side past one of those extreme cells would leave a `1` outside, so the best rectangle is the one whose four sides sit exactly on those four extremes. Trying every possible rectangle also works, but one pass over the cells is enough to find the extremes.

## Approach

1. Start `top` and `left` past the far edge of the grid and `bottom` and `right` at `-1`, so the first `1` found sets all four.
2. Visit every cell by `row` and `col`.
3. For each cell holding `1`, pull `top` and `left` down to its row and column with `Math.min`, and push `bottom` and `right` up with `Math.max`.
4. The rectangle spans `height = bottom - top + 1` rows and `width = right - left + 1` columns; return `height * width`.

## Example 1, step by step

`grid = [[0,1,0],[1,0,1]]` starts with `top = 2`, `bottom = -1`, `left = 3`, `right = -1`.
- The `1` at row 0, column 1 sets `top = 0`, `bottom = 0`, `left = 1`, `right = 1`.
- The `1` at row 1, column 0 sets `bottom = 1` and `left = 0`.
- The `1` at row 1, column 2 sets `right = 2`.

So `height = 1 - 0 + 1 = 2`, `width = 2 - 0 + 1 = 3`, and the area is `6`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(m·n): every cell is read once.
- Space: O(1): four bounds and two sizes.

## Pitfalls

- The bounds are inclusive cell indices, so each side length needs `+ 1`; `bottom - top` alone undercounts.
- The rows and columns are tracked separately: the topmost and leftmost `1` are usually different cells.
- Starting `top` at `0` (instead of past the edge) would make `Math.min` keep it at `0` forever.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `top`, `bottom` | smallest and largest row index holding a `1` |
| `left`, `right` | smallest and largest column index holding a `1` |
| `row`, `col` | the cell being read |
| `height`, `width` | the rows and columns the rectangle spans |

narration.2: Start the top bound below the last row so the first 1 always lowers it.
narration.3: Start the bottom bound above the first row so the first 1 always raises it.
narration.4: Likewise, the left bound starts past the last column...
narration.5: ...and the right bound before the first column.
narration.7: Scan the rows from top to bottom.
narration.8: Scan each row's cells from left to right.
narration.9: Only cells holding a 1 must fit inside the rectangle.
narration.10: The rectangle's top can be no lower than this row.
narration.11: Its bottom can be no higher than this row.
narration.12: Its left side can be no further right than this column.
narration.13: Its right side can be no further left than this column.
narration.17: The bounds are inclusive, so the row count is the difference plus one.
narration.18: The same holds for the column count.
narration.19: The tightest rectangle's area is its height times its width.
